q.t: Find the adjective: She wore a red dress.
q.e: ‘red’ tells what kind of dress.

q.t: Find the adjective: The water is cold.
q.e: After the linking verb ‘is’, ‘cold’ describes the water.

q.t: Comparative of tall:
q.e: One-syllable word → add -er.

q.t: Superlative of good:
q.e: good is irregular: good, better, best.

q.t: Comparative of big:
q.e: Short vowel + single consonant → double it: bigger (otherwise it would sound like ‘biger’ rhyming with tiger).

q.t: Comparative of happy:
q.e: Consonant + y → change y to i and add -er.

q.t: Superlative of beautiful:
q.e: Long word → use ‘most’.

q.t: Fill in: An elephant is ___ than a horse.
q.e: Two things compared with ‘than’ → comparative.

q.t: Fill in: Riya is the ___ girl in the class.
q.e: One out of the whole class (more than two) → superlative with ‘the’.

q.t: Which is an adjective of number?
q.e: ‘five’ tells how many.

q.t: Superlative of bad:
q.e: bad is irregular: bad, worse, worst.

q.t: Comparative of little (amount):
q.e: little, less, least (for amounts).

q.t: Fill in: This is the ___ of the two pens.
q.e: Only two pens are being compared, so use the comparative even with ‘the’.

q.t: Find the error: She is more cleverer than her brother.
q.e: -er already means ‘more’. Using both is a double comparative.

q.t: Fill in: I have ___ money left, so I can buy a snack.
q.e: Money is uncountable. ‘a little’ = some, enough (positive). ‘little’ would mean almost none.

q.t: Fill in: He has ___ friends, so he often feels lonely.
q.e: ‘friends’ is countable, and lonely shows the negative sense ‘almost none’ → few.

q.t: Which word is an adjective? This bag is mine.
q.e: ‘This’ points out which bag — a demonstrative adjective (it comes before the noun).

q.t: Fill in: Which is the ___ river in India?
q.e: One out of many rivers → superlative. ‘long’ is one syllable → -est.

q.t: Comparative of hot:
q.e: Short vowel + one consonant → double the t.

q.t: Which is NOT an adjective of quantity?
q.e: ‘three’ counts things — an adjective of number. The others tell amount.

q.t: Change to comparative: Gold is the most precious metal.
o: Gold is more precious than any other metal.
Gold is more precious than any metal.
Gold is precious than other metals.
No metal is more precious than gold is.
q.e: Use ‘any other’ — gold is itself a metal and cannot be more precious than itself.

q.t: Change to positive: Ravi is the cleverest boy in the class.
o: No other boy in the class is as clever as Ravi.
Ravi is as clever as the other boys in the class.
No boy in the class is cleverer than Ravi is.
Ravi is not as clever as other boys in the class.
q.e: Positive degree uses ‘as … as’. ‘No other boy is as clever as Ravi’ keeps him at the top.

q.t: Choose the correct order: a ___ table
q.e: Opinion (beautiful) → age (old) → material (wooden).

q.t: Choose the correct order: She bought a ___ scarf.
q.e: Opinion → size → material.

q.t: Fill in: Of all the students, Meera is the ___.
q.e: ‘Of all’ → superlative. Long word → ‘most’.

q.t: Find the error: This is the most easiest sum.
q.e: -est already means ‘most’. Use only one: easiest.

q.t: Choose the correct word: Let us not walk any ___. (more distance)
q.e: far → farther/further. ‘further’ is also fine; ‘farer’ is not a word.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He is more senior than me.
q.e: Latin comparatives (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) take ‘to’, not ‘than’.

q.t: Fill in: The ___ you study, the ___ you learn.
q.e: ‘The more …, the more …’ — two comparatives show that one grows with the other.

q.t: Which sentence uses an adjective after a linking verb?
q.e: ‘smells’ links the soup to a quality (delicious) — so an adjective, not an adverb, follows it.

q.t: Change to superlative: No other planet is as big as Jupiter.
o: Jupiter is bigger than other planets.
Jupiter is as big as other planets.
q.e: If no planet matches it, Jupiter is at the top — the biggest.

q.t: Change to comparative: Very few cities in India are as old as Varanasi.
o: Varanasi is older than most other cities in India.
Varanasi is older than any other city in India.
Varanasi is the oldest city in India.
Varanasi is not older than other cities in India.
q.e: ‘Very few are as old’ means some others are equally old, so it is ‘older than MOST other cities’ — not ‘any other’ and not ‘the oldest’.

q.t: Find the error: He is the best of the two players.
q.e: With only two, use the comparative: the better of the two.

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I prefer tea more than coffee.
I more prefer tea to coffee.
q.e: ‘prefer’ already means ‘like better’, so it takes ‘to’, never ‘than’ or ‘more’.

q.t: Choose the correct order: a ___ ring
q.e: Size → shape → material.

q.t: Fill in: Of the two sisters, Meena is the ___.
q.e: Two sisters → comparative. For family members ‘elder’ is used before nouns or with ‘the’ (the elder sister).

q.t: Choose the correct word: There were ___ people at the meeting than we expected.
q.e: People are countable → fewer. Use ‘less’ for amounts you cannot count (less water).

q.t: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Delhi is larger than any other city in this list.
Delhi is larger than any city in this list.
Delhi is the larger than any other city.
Delhi is most larger city in this list.
q.e: Delhi is in the list, so ‘any other’ — otherwise Delhi would be compared with itself.

q.t: What does She has little hope of winning. mean?
o: She has a lot of hope.
q.e: ‘little’ without ‘a’ is negative: hardly any. ‘a little hope’ would mean some hope.

q.t: Choose the correct option: This road is ___ dangerous than the old one.
q.e: ‘less’ + adjective makes the opposite of ‘more’: less dangerous. ‘fewer’ is only for countable nouns.
